title: Nucleic Acids and Nucleotides
objectives: Understand the structure and components of nucleotides
Describe the chemical properties and biological roles of DNA and RNA
Explain the processes of DNA replication, transcription, and translation
Analyze the metabolic pathways involving nucleotide synthesis and degradation

overview.title: Nucleic Acid Overview
overview.content:
Nucleic acids are biopolymers essential for all known forms of life, consisting of nucleotides as their monomeric units. There are two main types: deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) which stores genetic information, and ribonucleic acid (RNA) which plays various roles in protein synthesis and gene regulation. Nucleotides also serve as energy carriers (ATP), cofactors (NAD), and signaling molecules (cAMP).

Biological Significance

  • Genetic Information: DNA encodes the instructions for development, functioning, and reproduction.
  • Protein Synthesis: RNA translates genetic information into proteins.
  • Energy Metabolism: ATP is the primary energy currency of cells.
  • Cellular Signaling: Nucleotides participate in intracellular and extracellular signaling.

Key Components

Nucleotide Structure

  • Nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine)
  • Pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose)
  • Phosphate group (1-3)

Nucleic Acid Types

  • DNA (double-stranded, deoxyribose, thymine)
  • RNA (single-stranded, ribose, uracil)
  • mRNA, tRNA, rRNA (protein synthesis)

key_concepts.title: Key Concepts
key_concepts.content:
Base Pairing Rules

DNA: Adenine (A) pairs with Thymine (T), Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C).

RNA: Adenine (A) pairs with Uracil (U), Guanine (G) pairs with Cytosine (C).

Phosphodiester Bonds

Formation: Covalent bonds between the 3' hydroxyl of one nucleotide and the 5' phosphate of another.

Significance: Forms the sugar-phosphate backbone of nucleic acids.

DNA vs. RNA

DNA: Stable, double-stranded, stores genetic information long-term.

RNA: Less stable, single-stranded, diverse functional roles.

chemical_properties.title: Chemical Properties
chemical_properties.content:
Hydrogen Bonding

Base Pairing: A-T/U forms 2 hydrogen bonds, G-C forms 3 hydrogen bonds.

Acid-Base Properties

Phosphate Groups: Make nucleic acids negatively charged at physiological pH.

UV Absorption

Characteristic: Nucleic acids absorb UV light at 260 nm due to aromatic bases.

Application: Used to quantify and assess purity of nucleic acid samples.

biological_roles.title: Biological Roles
biological_roles.content:
Information Storage and Transfer

Replication: DNA makes identical copies of itself during cell division.

Transcription: DNA is transcribed into RNA.

Translation: mRNA is translated into proteins.

Energy and Metabolism

ATP: Primary energy currency of cells.

NAD+/FAD: Electron carriers in redox reactions.

Regulation

Gene Expression: microRNAs regulate gene expression.

Signaling: cAMP and cGMP act as second messengers.

faqs.title: FAQs
faqs.content:
Why does DNA contain thymine while RNA contains uracil?+
Thymine provides more stability for long-term information storage, while uracil's presence in RNA allows for more flexibility and degradation when needed.
What gives DNA its double helical structure?+
Hydrogen bonding between complementary bases and hydrophobic interactions between stacked base pairs stabilize the double helix.
How do antiparallel strands affect DNA replication?+
Antiparallel orientation requires different mechanisms for copying each strand (leading and lagging strand synthesis).
What's the difference between a nucleoside and nucleotide?+
A nucleoside consists of a base and sugar only, while a nucleotide has one or more phosphate groups added to the nucleoside.
